expectations.text: Advises starting coarser / not pre-splitting the three phases into many files up front
expectations.evidence: Proposes a heavily pre-split layout (~18 files across api/services/csv/jobs folders) on day one, splitting the lifecycle into create-export.ts / get-export-status.ts / process-export.ts and CSV into generate-csv/escape/columns. The 'don't over-build the seams' caveat applies only to DI/repository abstractions, not to the file fragmentation itself.

expectations.text: Co-locates tightly coupled job lifecycle / polling
expectations.evidence: Job lifecycle deliberately split into separate service files; "Split the job concerns from the CSV concerns" and one verb per file — the opposite of co-locating the coupled lifecycle.

expectations.text: Recommends an abstraction (function/module) over bare file splits
expectations.evidence: "Wrap the queue behind an adapter (jobs/queue.ts)"; "A JobStatus state machine"; "index.ts as the public contract."

expectations.text: Mentions a ~300-line threshold (or 'a few hundred lines') as the split trigger
expectations.evidence: "Keep files small — roughly under ~200 lines." Falls within 'a few hundred lines' as a size threshold.
